Running command: cd /workspace && cat > candidate_trace.json <<'JSON'
[
  {"step":1,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":128,"var":"psf_header","code":"psf_binheader_readf (psf, \"pb\", 0, psf_header, NIST_HEADER_LENGTH) ;","note":"Attacker-controlled NIST bytes are copied from the input file into the fixed-size header buffer for parsing."},
  {"step":2,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":131,"var":"psf_header[NIST_HEADER_LENGTH]","code":"psf_header [NIST_HEADER_LENGTH] = 0 ;","note":"The parser null-terminates the copied header so later string operations treat it as a C string."},
  {"step":3,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":148,"var":"count","code":"if (sscanf (psf_header, \"NIST_1A\\n%d\\n\", &count) == 1)","note":"The declared header length is read from the attacker-controlled header and used to set the data offset."},
  {"step":4,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":166,"var":"psf->bytewidth","code":"if ((cptr = strstr (psf_header, \"sample_n_bytes -i \")) != NULL) sscanf (cptr, \"sample_n_bytes -i %d\", &(psf->bytewidth)) ;","note":"The sample byte width is parsed from the header and stored for later format decisions."},
  {"step":5,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":171,"var":"psf->endian","code":"if ((cptr = strstr (psf_header, \"sample_byte_format -s\")) && sscanf (cptr, \"sample_byte_format -s%u %8s\", &bytes, str) == 2)","note":"The byte-order field is parsed from the attacker-controlled header and may change the file format state."},
  {"step":6,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":188,"var":"psf->sf.format","code":"psf->sf.format |= psf->endian ;","note":"The parsed endian choice is merged into the format, completing header interpretation before data access."},
  {"step":7,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":224,"var":"psf->blockwidth","code":"psf->blockwidth = psf->sf.channels * psf->bytewidth ;","note":"The parsed channel count and byte width are combined into the block size used by later reads."},
  {"step":8,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_read_header","line":227,"var":"psf->dataoffset","code":"psf_fseek (psf, psf->dataoffset, SEEK_SET) ;","note":"The parser seeks to the attacker-specified data offset, positioning the stream at the sample payload."},
  {"step":9,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/nist.c","function":"nist_open","line":96,"var":"encoding","code":"if ((error = nist_read_header (psf))) return error ;","note":"Opening the file invokes the header parser; a malformed header can steer later state into the vulnerable path."},
  {"step":10,"file":"src-vul/libsndfile/src/common.c","function":"psf_binheader_readf","line":1010,"var":"count","code":"case 'b' : /* Raw bytes */ charptr = va_arg (argptr, char*) ; count = va_arg (argptr, size_t) ; memset (charptr, 0, count) ; byte_count += header_read (psf, charptr, count) ;","note":"The raw-byte read helper copies the attacker-controlled header into the destination buffer, but the vulnerability is triggered later when the parsed header state is consumed without fully initializing all dependent fields."}
]
JSON
